openrouter._notes: One key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY) covers every model below. Prices are read live from GET /models, which is public and unauthenticated — run `python src/probe_models.py` to re-verify every slug and see the current price before spending money. OpenRouter is asked for usage.include so each run returns the ACTUAL dollars it cost; manifest.csv records that rather than our estimate.
openrouter._budget: Arms A/B/E only (C and D still defined in itemloader.ARMS, excluded via enabled_arms). reps 3/4: coding+knowledge 3 reps, agentic 4 reps -> 342 runs. Modelled cost: $2.66 low / $8.16 mid / $23.47 high. Planned against $14.00 usable (6000 HUF less 5.5% credit fee and likely 27% AFA). Run with --budget 14 as a hard stop.
openrouter._fees: OpenRouter charges NO markup on inference (provider prices pass through) but a 5.5% platform fee on credit purchases (Standard tier), $0.80 minimum. Crypto is 5%. A Business tier at 8% exists and routes EU-only. Hungarian AFA at 27% may apply on top — check the live checkout total, the published percentage is not the final charge. Budget is therefore planned at $14.00 usable out of 6000 HUF, not the $18.73 the rate implies.

notes: 6 models, AA Intelligence Index 13.7 -> 45, three arms A/B/E. Nemotron 3 Ultra dropped on cost; MiMo-V2.6-Pro dropped as slow and expensive (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor covers the top of the axis at a fifth of the price). NOTE: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's price on OpenRouter moved from $0.035/$0.290 to $0.30/$1.20 between probes — the probe caught it, which is what the probe is for. Prices drift; re-run python src/probe_models.py before spending. Arms C and D are still defined in src/itemloader.ARMS but excluded via enabled_arms — the study is scoped to one question: is it better to ASK the user (B) or to STATE assumptions and be corrected (E), against an unanswered baseline (A).

simulator.why: 25000. The simulator is reasoning-first (deepseek-v4-pro) and a small cap let it spend the whole budget on thinking and return EMPTY content -- 42% of turns on the 2026-09-29 run were silent, and the old fallback then told the test model 'that's all fine', handing it an unearned pass. Generous budget so the reply always survives.

arms.B: Before you start, ask me up to 4 questions. Do NOT start the task yet and do NOT produce any output for it — ask your questions and stop. If I don't answer something later, state what you assumed instead.
arms.C: Complete the task, using this specification: {spec}
arms.D: Do not ask me any questions. Before you start, list every assumption you are making about this task. Then complete the task.
arms.E: Do not ask me any questions. List every assumption you are making about this task — what I want, what was left unspecified, and what I might object to. Do NOT start the task yet and do NOT produce any output for it — list the assumptions and stop.

no_info_followup: No further information is available. Please complete the task.
capability_fingerprint: What is the capital of Australia? Answer with the city name only.
In what year did the Berlin Wall fall? Answer with the year only.
What is the derivative of x^3 with respect to x? Answer with the expression only.
Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'? Answer with the surname only.
What is the chemical symbol for gold? Answer with the symbol only.
disclosures: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor: heavily discounted pricing in exchange for permission to use prompts and completions to train future Meta models. Recorded because it is a data-for-price trade and raises a contamination question for replication.
Muse Spark 1.3's AA index of 45 is measured at the 'xhigh' reasoning-effort tier; the tier actually used is recorded per model in effort_tier.
OpenRouter may route to different upstream providers per request; the provider actually serving each call is recorded from the response when available.

All six models are served through one endpoint (OpenRouter) with one identical three-tool set (list_dir / read_file / write_file), so the serving stack is constant across the capability axis — provider differences cannot confound the capability comparison.

Arm E cannot fully separate assumption externalisation from additional deliberation (both add tokens before the artifact). Mitigation: IA and AE are scored separately and H2' predicts only IA moves. If only AE improves, the 'just more compute' explanation wins.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro (index 46) and Nemotron 3 Ultra (index 47.7) were dropped on cost. The axis therefore ends at 45, so behaviour above ~45 is unobserved and the true capability ceiling (Claude Opus 5.5 at 58) is out of reach — a limitation, not a result.
